item.title: The Paddle Generation: Why Breakout Never Died
item.dc:creator: Mara Voss
item.description: Why the paddle-and-ball formula keeps getting reinvented, from arcades to your browser tab.
item.content:encoded:
There is a quiet lineage of games that all share one shape: a paddle, a ball, and a wall of bricks. Breakout is the obvious starting point, but the lineage runs much deeper.

Three reinventions

  1. The arcade original — fixed screens, coin economics.
  2. The home console era — power-ups and destructible walls.
  3. The browser era — vector graphics, zero install, infinite lives for the curious.

What survives in each reinvention is the same three-second promise: you understand it instantly, and the skill ceiling is still there.

item.title: How We Measured 60 FPS in a 2025 Browser
item.description: A methodology post from the archive.
item.content:encoded:
Frame timing in the browser is easier than it looks, and much more interesting than people assume. We used requestAnimationFrame deltas over a 10-second window, bucketed into 4ms bins, and reported the 95th percentile.

The result on our reference hardware: median 16.6ms, p95 17.1ms. The long tail is almost always layout, not rendering.

Full methodology in the appendix of the original post.
